claim: Omdia estimated that four companies, which it describes only as memory suppliers and Nvidia (not named individually), together raised their share of semiconductor revenue from 24% in 2023 to 42% in 2025, and that top-ten company revenue grew 90% over 2023-2025 versus 8% for the rest of the market.
evidence: "revenue among the top ten semiconductor companies increased by 90% compared with 8% growth across the remainder of the market. Omdia says growth has been concentrated among memory suppliers and NVIDIA, highlighting how significantly AI demand is shaping the semiconductor market. Combined, these four companies increased their share of total semiconductor revenue from 24% in 2023 to 42% in 2025." (MacTech republication of Omdia, 24 Mar 2026, section 'Revenue consolidation among leading companies')

metric.name: Share of semiconductor revenue held by four companies (memory suppliers and Nvidia, per Omdia)
metric.population: Omdia semiconductor revenue; the three memory suppliers are not named by the source

notes: Corrects CLM-0721, which named Samsung, SK hynix and Micron although the source does not.

claim: Gartner's upgrade to Nvidia's 2024 revenue between its preliminary (US$46.0bn) and final (US$76.7bn) estimates, +US$30.7bn, was about the same size as the whole upgrade to its 2024 market total (US$626bn to US$655.9bn, +US$29.9bn), so other vendors' revisions netted to roughly zero.
evidence: Preliminary: "Worldwide semiconductor revenue in 2024 totaled $626 billion, an increase of 18.1% from 2023", Nvidia 45,988 US$M (Gartner, 3 Feb 2025); final: "Worldwide semiconductor revenue totaled $655.9 billion in 2024", NVIDIA 76,692 US$M (Gartner, April 2025, republished). 76.692-45.988 = 30.704; 655.9-626 = 29.9.
notes: Inference from CLM-0053, CLM-0054, CLM-0705. Netting to zero does not rule out larger offsetting revisions among other vendors; Gartner gave no explanation.
